explain.say: Imagine a painting that is also a map, a story and a lesson, all at once. That is what many Aboriginal paintings from Australia are. Aboriginal peoples have one of the oldest living cultures on Earth. Look at the timeline: art drawn in sand, on bodies and on rock goes back to ancient times.

explain.say: Look at 1971. At Papunya, a community in the Western Desert, a group of Aboriginal men painted a mural on their school wall, helped by a young teacher called Geoffrey Bardon. Soon they were painting on boards and canvas, and dot painting became famous. Why do you think painting on canvas let more people see the art?

explain.say: So why the dots? Look at the board. Some stories hold sacred knowledge meant only for certain people. Covering the designs with dots can share a story with the world while keeping the secret parts private. Isn't that a clever, respectful idea?

faq.a: Dot painting is a style of art developed by Aboriginal artists of Australia's Western Desert, where designs and symbols are built up from many dots of paint. The paintings often tell stories about Country, ancestors and law.
asks: Why is Aboriginal art made of dots?

faq.a: The modern dot painting movement began in 1971 at Papunya, in Australia's Northern Territory, when Aboriginal men painted a mural at the school, encouraged by teacher Geoffrey Bardon.

faq.q: What do the symbols in dot paintings mean?
faq.a: Some symbols are widely shared, like circles for a waterhole or camp, U shapes for people and lines for journeys. But meanings depend on the artist and community, and some are not explained to outsiders.
asks: What does a circle mean in Aboriginal art?
What does a U shape mean in Aboriginal art?

faq.q: Why do Aboriginal artists use dots?
faq.a: Dots echo designs made in sand and on bodies for ceremonies, and they can cover sacred details, so a painting can be shared publicly while secret knowledge stays protected.
asks: Why use dots instead of lines?

faq.q: How can I enjoy Aboriginal art respectfully?
faq.a: Learn the artist's name and community, do not copy sacred designs or claim them as your own, and buy from Aboriginal-owned art centres so artists are paid fairly.
asks: Is it OK to copy Aboriginal art?
Where should I buy Aboriginal art?

facts: The modern Western Desert dot painting movement began at Papunya in 1971.
A painting of a kangaroo in the Kimberley region of Western Australia has been dated to about 17,300 years old, the oldest known intact rock painting in Australia.
Emily Kame Kngwarreye, an Anmatyerre artist, became one of Australia's most celebrated painters in the 1990s.
